I'm 47, never went to school, not even one day. I've been farming these 10 mu 9 fen for 30 years — since I was 17 and my old man handed me the hoe. We got four mouths at home: my wife picks up odd jobs in town at a garment workshop when they have work, my father's nearly 70 and can't do heavy lifting no more, and my son is pouring concrete over in Shijiazhuang. So it's mostly me and the old man on the land now.

I keep about 8 mu for wheat-maize double crop — that's my backbone, guarantees I have grain to eat and some to sell. The other 2 mu 9 fen I plant cotton. Can't do more cotton, it's too much work for picking and the price jumps around like a rabbit. But cotton brings cash when the price is decent, so I keep that bit.

The wheat went in last October, around the 15th. I used my own saved seed — buying new certified seed costs 30-40 yuan a mu, and my own seed sprouts fine. For the base fertilizer I spread one big 50kg bag of compound fertilizer per mu, plus another half bag. That's what I've always done, what my father did. Now it's spring, the wheat's turning green. I need to water it for the returning-green stage, and I'll spread about 10 jin of urea per mu — roughly half a small bag. If the wheat looks yellow at jointing, maybe I'll throw another 5 jin, but fertilizer is expensive now, over 100 yuan a bag, so I don't want to go crazy. Last year Old Zhang from the east end tried to save money on fertilizer and his wheat came up thin — I'm not making that mistake. Water — I'll irrigate twice: returning-green and jointing. If it rains good in May I might skip the third. Every time I start that pump the electricity meter spins fast, and water fees keep going up.

Come June, soon as the wheat's cut — I hire the combine harvester, 50 yuan a mu but it's fast, finished in a morning — I plant maize that same week. No time to waste in double cropping. Maize seed I buy hybrid, about 40 yuan a mu, because hybrid maize grows stronger. Base fertilizer: half a big bag of compound per mu, about 25 kg. Then at the big trumpet stage I side-dress another 10 jin of urea. Maize I might water once in summer, twice if July turns scorching hot. I spray herbicide once after planting, and if I see corn borer worms I'll spray insecticide, but I don't go looking for trouble.

Cotton goes in late April on that 2 mu 9 fen. Cotton is a headache — aphids, bollworms, you name it. I plow and harrow the plot first, then plant. Base fertilizer is about one bag of compound per mu. I water twice, maybe three times if it's dry in July. I spray three, four times for sure — herbicide after planting, then insecticide when the bugs show up. The picking kills me — it's me, my wife, and my father crawling through the rows for weeks. I still have to hire women from the village to help pick, 100 to 120 yuan a day plus lunch. That's where the money bleeds out.

Everything costs more than five years ago. Fertilizer, electricity for water, hired labor for picking. I probably spend around 6,800 yuan on inputs for the whole year. My neighbor with 15 mu and two sons at home can afford more, but I'm stretched thin — my son needs money to get married, and I can't have a bad year. I expect wheat around 400-450 jin per mu, maize around 500 jin, cotton maybe 400 jin of seed cotton. If I hit those numbers, we'll have enough grain and a bit of cash left over. That's all I ask — not getting rich, just not falling behind.
